items.title: MetLife (MET) Agrees To Divest MetLife UK Limited
items.summary: MetLife (NYSE: MET) has agreed to sell MetLife UK Limited to life and pensions consolidator Chesnara. The proposed transaction will be subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to follow a multi year completion timeline. The deal marks a planned reduction of MetLife's UK presence as the insurer looks to concentrate on other international priorities. items.title: Chesnara CEO targets further deals after £1.7bn MetLife UK acquisition
items.summary:
Chesnara PLC (LSE:CSN) CEO Steve Murray spoke with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about the group’s agreement to acquire MetLife UK’s closed-book life insurance business, adding 18,000 policies and £1.7bn in assets under administration.

The deal, Chesnara’s fourth acquisition in two years, is expected to generate around £90m in lifetime cashflows and add approximately £45m to Own Funds and Contractual Service Margin. It is expected to complete in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

Murray said the portfolio was a strong fit with Chesnara’s existing UK operations, with administration already handled by its outsourcing partner SS&C Technologies. The acquisition is expected to have a broadly neutral impact on the group’s Solvency II ratio.

The discussion also covered Chesnara’s growing role as a consolidation partner for major financial institutions and its pipeline of potential deals. Murray outlined the investment in people and operational capacity needed to support further acquisitions, while maintaining the group’s record of 21 consecutive years of dividend growth.
